items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Replace HF3FS block table on MRV1 resume
items.body:
## Overview

Replace HF3FS's retained physical block table when an MRV1 request resumes from preemption. This applies the scheduler contract already used by MooncakeStore in #46595.

## Claims

- A resumed `CachedRequestData` table replaces the freed placement rather than being appended to it.
- An ordinary cached request still appends its allocation delta.
- Logical token history and the saved-content cursor are preserved in the cached-request path.

## Validation

Local CPU validation on 2026-10-12, base `8d7b93fec2eb`, candidate `db9127ecf56d`:

- Test-only exact-base control: **1 failed, 1 passed**. Resume retains `[10, 11, 20, 21, 22]` instead of `[20, 21, 22]`; ordinary append passes.
- Fixed contract selection, including the scheduler and MooncakeStore precedent: **5 passed**.
- HF3FS and MooncakeStore adjacent selection: **85 passed, 6 skipped, 8 deselected**. Skips need the real HF3FS client; deselected cases are the CUDA-dependent mock-client class.
- Complete connector file: **14 passed, 4 failed** versus base **12 passed, the same 4 failed**. All four are mock-client writes blocked by the missing NVIDIA driver, not additional failures introduced here.
- CPU CI marker selection: **2 passed, 16 deselected**.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks, including mypy and test tethering, and `git diff --check` passed.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py::test_mrv1_resume_replaces_reallocated_block_table \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py::test_running_request_appends_new_block_ids \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_cached_request_data_resumed_all_token_ids_mrv1_only \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py::test_running_request_not_in_resumed_req_ids_appends_blocks \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py::test_resumed_request_in_resumed_req_ids_replaces_blocks

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_client.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_metadata_server.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  -k 'not TestHf3fsMockClient'

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/hf3fs/hf3fs_connector.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/hf3fs/utils/common.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py
```

The CPU runs used the existing shared virtual environment, this checkout on `PYTHONPATH`, and `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.

**Serving validation, 2026-10-12:** one A40, Qwen3-0.6B at `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, BF16, MRV1 in-process engine, eager, no speculation or async scheduling, local APC disabled, 16-token blocks. Using HF3FS's file-backed fallback and a fresh local metadata server, force one genuine scheduler preemption and an external miss. Baseline retains 28 physical IDs (14 stale plus 14 replacement); fixed retains exactly the scheduler's 14 replacement IDs. Both have a later saved tail. Each arm completes 80 greedy tokens identical to the cold reference, **n=1 per arm**. Complete connector file on the same GPU: base **16 passed**, fixed **18 passed**, zero failures/errors/skips.

This is a fault-injected connector-serving check, not a deployed 3FS cluster, natural preemption-frequency measurement, hybrid/speculative validation or throughput claim. Reproduction used `serving_probe.py --case resume --arm base|fixed --head <pinned-head>` through an isolated local driver; raw JSON/logs and the harness are retained in the review packet.

## Details

The scheduler marks a cached request as resumed when `new_block_ids` contains its complete replacement table. HF3FS keeps scheduling state across preemption but previously appended that table to its old, freed physical IDs. Subsequent saves select physical sources positionally, leaving logical positions and physical placement inconsistent.

The change passes `resumed_req_ids` into the existing private update and replaces only the physical IDs. It adds 15 production lines across two connector-local files, no public API and no device synchronization. MRV2 resumes use `NewRequestData`; HF3FS's existing initializer already replaces their physical table. This patch targets the still-supported MRV1 cached-request representation, not a new MRV1 feature or complete source-lifetime protection.

**Related-work check, 2026-10-12:** open and closed HF3FS resume/preemption searches found no matching fix. Credit @ivanium's merged #46595 for the general invariant. #52837 proposes a broader record-driven save design. Open #49970 changes DCP geometry; #51748/#54342 change key identity; #55542 changes typing. #57777 renames save finalization. None implements this cached-request replacement. Concurrent changes to the same files may require a rebase.

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, validation and drafting.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Drain and validate HF3FS save writers
items.body:
## Overview

Drain every submitted HF3FS save writer before returning its shared staging buffers, and require complete allocation/write results before confirming cache keys.

## Claims

- An early writer failure or a later submission exception cannot bypass draining of previously submitted writers.
- Only one non-Boolean integer full-page result per submitted page authorizes confirmation; empty and truncated results fail.
- Malformed allocation replies fail before gathering KV. Failed saves do not release ownership-ambiguous page indices.

## Validation

Local CPU validation on 2026-10-12, base `8d7b93fec2eb`, candidate `d72b2fd212f4`:

- Focused save-completion suite: **22 passed**.
- Exact-base test-only control: **20 failed, 2 passed**. This count includes absent helper methods; it is not a claim of 20 distinct bugs.
- Restoring only the legacy write loop, while retaining the new helpers and allocation checks: **3 failed**. Both incomplete-result cases falsely succeed, and the lifetime case frees a buffer while a later writer is pending.
- Restoring the previous preliminary `concurrent.futures.wait` call: **1 failed** on a cancelled queued future. The drain now calls each future's `result()` directly, catches failure/cancellation and continues to every later writer.
- CPU-applicable HF3FS adjacent suite: **44 passed, 6 skipped, 8 deselected**. Skips need real HF3FS; the CUDA-dependent mock-client class is deselected.
- Complete connector file: **34 passed, 4 failed** versus base **12 passed, the same 4 failed**, all blocked by the missing NVIDIA driver.
- CPU CI marker selection: **22 passed, 16 deselected**.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks, including mypy and test tethering, and `git diff --check` passed.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py::TestHF3FSWriterCompletion

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_client.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_metadata_server.py \
  -k 'not TestHf3fsMockClient'

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/hf3fs/hf3fs_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py
```

The CPU runs used the existing shared virtual environment, this checkout on `PYTHONPATH`, and `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.

**Serving validation, 2026-10-12:** one A40, Qwen3-0.6B at `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, BF16, MRV1 in-process engine, eager, no speculation or async scheduling, local APC disabled, 16-token blocks. Using HF3FS's file-backed fallback, both arms first complete a successful real save. An injected first-batch failure holds a second accepted real writer pending: baseline returns shared buffers early, fixed does not; both report save failure. Each arm completes 80 greedy tokens identical to the cold reference, **n=1 per arm**. Complete connector file on the same GPU: base **16 passed**, fixed **38 passed**, zero failures/errors/skips.

This is a controlled connector-serving failure, not a deployed 3FS cluster, latency/throughput measurement, hybrid/speculative validation or proof of complete remediation. The writer hold is an intervention, not a benchmark. Reproduction used `serving_probe.py --case writers --arm base|fixed --head <pinned-head>` through an isolated local driver; raw JSON/logs and the harness are retained in the review packet.

## Details

The old nested `all(...)` short-circuits on the first bad write result, while later writers may still read the same staging buffers. A submission exception has the same lifetime problem. Empty/truncated result lists can also satisfy the old success check without proving all pages were written.

Two private helpers track batch sizes and drain every accepted future. Allocation validation checks key order, cardinality and unique nonnegative integer page indices before gathering. The change adds 85 production lines in one connector-local file and no public API or new main-thread device synchronization.

The current allocator can return an existing complete key's live page without identifying ownership. A failed save therefore retains raw page indices rather than guessing that they may be released. **This may leak newly allocated capacity on failure.** An accepted writer that never terminates keeps the save worker blocked; a timeout cannot safely authorize buffer reuse.

This is partial hardening, not the complete page-ownership or source-lifetime fix. It does not make overwriting an existing complete page transactional, protect source GPU blocks before gathering, fix loads, or change external key identity. Those need separate changes.

**Related-work check, 2026-10-12:** searches for HF3FS writers, batch writes, allocation and ownership found no matching fix. Open #49970 changes geometry; #51748/#54342 change keys; #55542 changes typing. #57777 renames the save-finalization method, while merged #57775 changes worker finalization scheduling. Neither drains or validates HF3FS writer futures. Concurrent changes to the same files may require a rebase.

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, validation and drafting.

items.title: [Metrics][Frontend] Pluggable KV connector metrics on the Rust frontend via connector metrics descriptor
items.body:
## Purpose

Today the Rust frontend's `/metrics` can only export KV connector metrics for Nixl and Mooncake, because each of them has dedicated Rust code. Stats from every other connector (Offloading, HF3FS, HiSparse, and out-of-tree connectors) do reach the Rust process, but are silently dropped, so these metrics disappear as soon as `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` is set.

This PR lets a connector describe its own metrics, so the Rust frontend can export them without any per-connector Rust code. Design discussion: RFC: #58562.

## Changes

How it works:

1. On the Rust frontend, the first time a connector reports stats, it also sends a short description of its metrics: name, type, help text, histogram buckets, and where each value sits in its stats. The description rides the existing scheduler stats message; there is no new RPC.
2. When the Rust frontend sees a description, it registers those metrics. After that, every stats tick carries values only, and Rust updates the metrics from them.
3. On the Python frontend nothing changes: no description is sent, and the existing Prometheus metrics stay as they are.
4. With MultiConnector, each child sends its own description and is exported separately.

Nixl and Mooncake keep their existing Rust code paths.

Key pieces:

- **`maybe_attach_metrics_descriptor()`** (Python): attaches the description once, and only when the Rust frontend is on. A connector calls it from its stats `to_dict()`.
- **Built-in connectors** (Python): Offloading, HF3FS, and HiSparse build their description from the same definitions their Prometheus metrics use; a unit test keeps the two in sync.
- **`DescriptorDrivenAdapter`** (Rust): registers metrics from a description and applies later values to them.
- **Routing in `metrics.rs`** (Rust): stats from connectors without dedicated Rust code go to the adapter, whose metrics are rendered on `/metrics` after the built-in ones.

- **Rust frontend zero-series pre-create:** once a connector metrics descriptor arrives, the Rust frontend pre-creates zero-valued series for every engine × model_name × const labels.
- **Rust HELP trailing-period strip:** when registering from a descriptor, the Rust frontend strips a single trailing `.` from HELP text before Prometheus adds its own, so HELP lines end with one period (matching the Python frontend).
- **List-valued gauge samples:** when a gauge's stats value is a list (HiSparse reports per-step lists), the Rust frontend sets the gauge to the last element, matching the Python Prometheus logger's last-value behavior.

An out-of-tree connector adopts this the same way: attach a description in its stats `to_dict()`.

> **NOTE:** On the Rust frontend, connector series are registered from the metrics descriptor carried on the first `SchedulerStats` that includes KV connector stats. Engine cores emit no stats while idle, so connector series appear after the connector first reports stats (then pre-created at 0 for all DP engines), rather than immediately at startup as on the Python frontend. The engine core was left untouched; a startup-only stats message from the core would close this gap but is not required for correct values after the first report.


## Known field differences (Rust vs Python)

These are field-level (name / HELP / TYPE / labels / suffixes), not value mismatches:

- **(a) Inherent encoder format:** Python's Prometheus client emits `_created` timestamps and names counters with a `_total` suffix in HELP/TYPE; the Rust encoder does not. Rust also pre-creates zero series after the first descriptor, so some families appear as samples earlier than on Python (where samples appear lazily after the first increment).
- **(b) Legacy / deprecated Python-only:** a few older Offloading families remain on the Python frontend only and are not part of the descriptor surface.
- **(c) Config-gated:** `stores_skipped` is always present in the Offloading descriptor (and therefore on Rust); the Python Prometheus path registers it only when `store_threshold >= 2`.
- **Nixl / Mooncake HELP punctuation:** on the Rust frontend, Nixl and Mooncake HELP strings still end with `..` because those connectors use the pre-existing typed Rust registration path, which is outside this PR; the trailing-period strip applies only to descriptor-registered metrics. The Python frontend's Nixl HELP lines end with a single `.`.
- **(d) Real adapter bugs:** none found in the paired field comparison across Offloading, HF3FS, HiSparse, OOT, and Multi.

## Test Plan

Unit tests:

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client connector_metrics
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_metrics_descriptor_emit.py
```

E2E: for each connector, start `vllm serve` with that connector, scrape `/metrics`, send a few requests, then scrape again. Each case runs on both frontends; the two runs differ only in `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`.

- Rust frontend passes if the connector's metrics appear on `/metrics` and update after the requests.
- Python frontend passes if no description is emitted and the metrics are the same as before this change.

<details>
<summary>E2E commands</summary>

Every case uses `--load-format dummy`. The Python and Rust frontend runs are identical except that the Rust run sets `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`. `<OutOfTreeConnector>` / `<out_of_tree_pkg>` stand for the out-of-tree connector used in the test.

```bash
# Rust frontend only:
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1

# Traffic and scrape (same for every case)
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics > before.txt
PREFIX=$(python3 -c 'print("token block cache reuse " * 80)')
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"model\":\"$MODEL\",\"prompt\":\"$PREFIX req $i\",\"max_tokens\":16,\"temperature\":0}"
done
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics > after.txt
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/models   # owned_by: vllm-frontend-rs (Rust) / vllm (Python)
```

**Offloading**

```bash
MODEL=moonshotai/Kimi-K3  # config reduced to 4 layers / 8 experts so it fits one GPU with dummy weights
vllm serve $MODEL --trust-remote-code --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":1073741824}}'
```

**HF3FS**

```bash
python3 -m vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hf3fs.hf3fs_metadata_server \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18000 &
MODEL=Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
vllm serve $MODEL --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HF3FSKVConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"hf3fs_storage_path":"/tmp/hf3fs_mock",
      "hf3fs_file_size":1073741824,"hf3fs_metadata_server_url":"http://127.0.0.1:18000"}}'
```

**HiSparse**

```bash
export VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip
MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2
vllm serve $MODEL --trust-remote-code --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
  --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 8}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":4}}'
```

**Out-of-tree connector**: same `vllm serve` flags as Offloading, with

```bash
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"<OutOfTreeConnector>",
  "kv_connector_module_path":"<out_of_tree_pkg>","kv_role":"kv_both"}'
```

**MultiConnector (Offloading + out-of-tree)**: same flags as Offloading, with

```bash

  "kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
    {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
     "kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":1073741824}},
    {"kv_connector":"<OutOfTreeConnector>","kv_connector_module_path":"<out_of_tree_pkg>",
     "kv_role":"kv_both"}]}}'
```

**MultiConnector (Nixl + out-of-tree), 1 prefill + 1 decode**

```bash
export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS   # needed for Nixl with this hybrid model
MODEL=moonshotai/Kimi-K3  # config reduced to 4 layers / 8 experts so it fits one GPU with dummy weights
multi() {  # $1 = kv_producer | kv_consumer
  echo '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"'$1'",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
      {"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"'$1'"},
      {"kv_connector":"<OutOfTreeConnector>","kv_connector_module_path":"<out_of_tree_pkg>",
       "kv_role":"kv_both"}]}}'
}
FLAGS="--trust-remote-code --load-format dummy --enforce-eager --max-model-len 2048 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align"
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5610 \
  vllm serve $MODEL $FLAGS --port 8100 --kv-transfer-config "$(multi kv_producer)" &
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5620 \
  vllm serve $MODEL $FLAGS --port 8200 --kv-transfer-config "$(multi kv_consumer)" &

# Per request: prefill on :8100 with max_tokens=1 and
#   "kv_transfer_params":{"do_remote_decode":true},
# then send the same prompt to :8200 with the kv_transfer_params returned by prefill.
# Scrape /metrics on both instances.
```

</details>

## Test Result

Unit tests: all pass.

| Connector | Rust frontend | Python frontend |
|-----------|---------------|-----------------|
| Offloading | PASS | PASS |
| HF3FS | PASS | PASS |
| HiSparse | PASS* | PASS* |
| Out-of-tree connector | PASS | PASS |
| MultiConnector (Offloading + out-of-tree) | PASS | PASS |
| MultiConnector (Nixl + out-of-tree, 1P1D) | PASS | PASS |
| DP=2 zero-series pre-create (Offloading; Multi+OOT) | PASS† | PASS (at startup) |

\* HiSparse metrics (3 counters and the 2 gauges `host_cache_usage_perc` / `pending_page_transfers`) are registered on both frontends, but the values stay at zero because dummy-weight traffic never reads from the host pool.

† Rust: connector series absent before the first request; after one request, zero-valued series exist for every DP engine. Python: series present at startup. See collapsed metrics excerpt below.

On the Python frontend, the metric names, help text, and types for Offloading and HF3FS are identical to `main`, and no `_metrics_descriptor` appears in `/metrics` or the logs. In the Nixl + out-of-tree case, the Nixl metrics keep coming from the existing Rust code path while the out-of-tree metrics come from the descriptor, and no warnings about unregistered or mismatched children are logged.

`/metrics` after traffic, filtered to each connector's metrics (out-of-tree metric prefix renamed to `oot_`):

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix HF3FS DCP block span
items.body:
## Purpose

The HF3FS KV connector currently hashes, counts, and aligns global token prefixes with the physical cache page size. Under DCP, one scheduler attention block ID spans `cache_config.block_size * dcp_world_size` global tokens, so the connector creates multiple storage keys for each allocated device block.

With a 16-token cache page and DCP=2, a complete 32-token prefix has one block ID. The current code creates two keys, one for tokens 0 through 15 and one for tokens 0 through 31, but provides only one device page. This key-to-page mismatch breaks save accounting, and the same physical-size conversion affects lookup, allocation validation, and load metadata.

This change uses the DCP-effective block size for token hashing and scheduler-side geometry. The worker continues to use `_local_block_size`, derived from the tensor shape, for device addresses and transfer-buffer sizes. It also adds a regression test to the existing HF3FS connector test file for the one-key-per-allocated-block invariant under DCP.

### Duplicate-work check

I searched open and closed issues and PRs for HF3FS, DCP, decode context parallelism, storage-key counts, and block-size mismatches.
I found no matching report or fix. The original HF3FS implementation in #37636 does not discuss DCP.

## Test plan

```bash
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py
```

## Test results

- Before the fix, the focused reproduction creates two storage keys for one allocated block ID.
- After the fix, it submits one key for one block ID.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py`: `17 passed`.

items.title: [Security] Include cache_salt in HF3FS external cache keys
items.body:
## Summary

HF3FS external cache keys were derived from token IDs alone and omitted the per-request `cache_salt`. Engines sharing an HF3FS metadata service could therefore alias the same exact prefix across different salts and expose cached-prefix membership through hit observability.

This change:

- carries `cache_salt` through scheduler state and HF3FS worker metadata;
- injects the salt into the first full-block hash so chained descendant hashes remain isolated;
- uses the salted keys consistently for metadata lookup, save, and load; and
- adds CPU-only production-path tests for A-hit/B-miss isolation and save/load key agreement.

items.title: [Bugfix] Partition HF3FS external cache keys by multimodal and LoRA identity
items.body:
## Overview

`HF3FSKVConnector` keys its external cache on `md5(prompt token ids)`. Two requests that differ
only in their image, their LoRA adapter or their `cache_salt` get the same keys, so the external
store can serve one request's KV blocks to the other. This PR keys the store on the engine's own
`request.block_hashes`, which already include those dimensions. Related: #51748, #53194, #53769.

## Claims

- **Bug:** external keys collide across multimodal content, LoRA identity and `cache_salt`.
  Multimodal placeholder tokens are the same for every image, so any two images that expand to
  the same number of tokens collide.
- **Root cause:** `_compute_prefix_hash` hashes `f"{previous_hash}_{token_ids}"` and nothing
  else. The lookup in `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, the save path and the load path all use it.
- **Fix:** a helper `external_block_keys()` takes `request.block_hashes` through
  `resolve_block_hashes` at the scheduler block size (from `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, which
  differs from `cache_config.block_size` for hybrid models and `dcp > 1`). The keys reach the
  worker in `HF3FSRequestMetadata.block_keys`. The MD5 derivation is removed. The engine builds
  the block hasher whenever a KV connector is configured, prefix caching on or off.

## Validation

Two requests that differ in exactly one dimension, block size 16, two full blocks, on the stock
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0` image (probe in the collapsed section, CPU only, no 3FS client;
the same keys were measured on 0.26.0):

| dimension | engine block hash | HF3FS external key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| multimodal content | different | **same** (`71cb373190a3aac9`) |
| LoRA identity | different | **same** (`71cb373190a3aac9`) |
| `cache_salt` | different | **same** (`71cb373190a3aac9`) |

the behavioural evidence for the stock code. The tests check that each dimension separates both
on the key and in the metadata the worker reads, that identical requests still share keys, that
a different second block leaves the first block's key unchanged, and that at
`block_size = 2 x hash_block_size` the coarse keys equal `[fine[1], fine[3]]`.

<summary>Probe used for the first table</summary>

```python
import json
from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash
from vllm.v1.request import Request
from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest
from vllm.multimodal.inputs import MultiModalFeatureSpec, MultiModalKwargsItem, PlaceholderRange
from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hf3fs.hf3fs_connector import (
    HF3FSKVConnector,
)

BLOCK = 16
init_none_hash(sha256)


def make_request(rid, token_ids, mm_hashes=None, cache_salt=None, lora=None):
    mm_features = None
    if mm_hashes:
        mm_features = [
            MultiModalFeatureSpec(
                data=MultiModalKwargsItem.dummy(),
                mm_position=PlaceholderRange(offset=0, length=len(token_ids)),
                identifier=h,
                modality="image",
            )
            for h in mm_hashes
        ]
    sp = SamplingParams(max_tokens=4)
    sp.update_from_generation_config({}, eos_token_id=100)
    return Request(
        request_id=rid,
        prompt_token_ids=list(token_ids),
        mm_features=mm_features,
        sampling_params=sp,
        pooling_params=None,
        lora_request=lora,
        cache_salt=cache_salt,
        block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(BLOCK, sha256),
    )


class _Hf3fsStub:
    _block_size = BLOCK
    _generate_block_hashes = HF3FSKVConnector._generate_block_hashes
    _compute_prefix_hash = HF3FSKVConnector._compute_prefix_hash


def keys(req):
    canonical = [bytes(h).hex()[:16] for h in req.block_hashes]
    external = _Hf3fsStub()._generate_block_hashes(list(req.prompt_token_ids), 0)
    return canonical, [e[:16] for e in external]


TOKENS = list(range(1000, 1000 + BLOCK * 2))
CASES = [
    ("multimodal content",
     make_request("a", TOKENS, mm_hashes=["image-of-a-cat"]),
     make_request("b", TOKENS, mm_hashes=["image-of-a-passport"])),
    ("LoRA identity",
     make_request("a", TOKENS, lora=LoRARequest("adapter-A", 1, "/tmp/a")),
     make_request("b", TOKENS, lora=LoRARequest("adapter-B", 2, "/tmp/b"))),
    ("cache_salt",
     make_request("a", TOKENS, cache_salt="tenant-1"),
     make_request("b", TOKENS, cache_salt="tenant-2")),
    ("control: different tokens",
     make_request("a", TOKENS),
     make_request("b", [t + 1 for t in TOKENS])),
    ("control: identical requests",
     make_request("a", TOKENS),
     make_request("b", TOKENS)),
]
for name, r1, r2 in CASES:
    c1, e1 = keys(r1)
    c2, e2 = keys(r2)
    print(json.dumps({"dimension": name,
                      "vllm_block_hash_separates": c1 != c2,
                      "hf3fs_external_key_separates": e1 != e2}))
```
</details>

## Details

- **#51748** (open) adds `cache_salt` alone to this connector. This PR covers `cache_salt` as a
  side effect of using the engine's hashes, and also covers multimodal and LoRA identity, which
  #51748 does not touch. The two will conflict textually; if #51748 lands first, the salt part
  of this PR becomes redundant, and the reverse also holds.
- **#53769** (open, conformance suite for #53194) now records this connector as
  `Keying.REDERIVES` but still exempts it as "needs the hf3fs client". The key derivation does
  not need the client: the test added here runs without it.
- **Other connectors:** native offloading, LMCache MP and Mooncake store already key on
  `request.block_hashes`. `ExampleConnector` has the same defect (#53495, open); #53496 (open)
  fixes it there the same way.
- **Key format change:** blocks that an older vLLM stored under the MD5 keys are not found
  after upgrading. They are recomputed and stored again under the new keys; no migration is
  attempted.
- **Cross-process keys:** with a cryptographic hash, `NONE_HASH` comes from a fixed seed, so
  separate processes agree on keys. With a non-cryptographic hash the seed is per-process
  (#12621) unless `PYTHONHASHSEED` is set. The old MD5 key had no such dependency.
- **Not a duplicate:** on 2026-10-03, and again on 2026-10-05, I searched open and merged PRs and issues for `hf3fs`,
  `HF3FSKVConnector`, `_generate_block_hashes` and `cache_salt`. #51748 is the only other PR on
  this connector's keys. #56643 and #58561 change the LMCache connector, not this one. `main`
  (`34051ad714`) and v0.31.0 still derive the key with `_generate_block_hashes`.
- **Limitations:** no 3FS cluster was available, so the connector was not run end to end. The
  evidence is at the level of the key derivation and the connector metadata.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Cap MooncakeStore lookup at num_tokens - 1
items.body:
---
## Summary

Caps the MooncakeStore lookup result at `num_tokens - 1` inside `MooncakeStoreScheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens`, so a lookup that reports the full prompt can no longer drive `num_new_tokens` to zero in `Scheduler.schedule()` and trip `assert num_new_tokens > 0` (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:923`) on the sync (`load_async=False`) path.

The cap is applied before both uses of the value, the returned `need_to_allocate` and the cached `load_specs.kvpool_cached_tokens`, so the round trip through the scheduler back into `update_state_after_alloc` (which asserts `num_external_tokens == kvpool_cached_tokens - vllm_cached_tokens`) stays consistent. No scheduler code is touched.

## Background

The last prompt token must always be recomputed locally to obtain logits. That rule is already enforced in three places: the local prefix cache lookup (`get_computed_blocks`), five in tree connectors (example, HF3FS, LMCache v1 adapter, MoRIIO READ, decode bench), and the MooncakeStore worker itself, which rederives a full hit below the request end (`worker.py:1854`). The MooncakeStore scheduler side component was the one place that passed the raw lookup count through uncapped.

One precision note for reviewers: through a matched pair of in tree server and scheduler components, the worker side rederivation keeps the lookup below N today. This change caps the scheduler side component itself, so the assert gated sync path no longer depends on server side behavior. The scheduler side receives its number over ZMQ from a server the base connector contract does not bound, and any server returning N (a third party implementation, a custom `LookupKeyServer`, or a future refactor) would crash `schedule()` without this guard.

## The fix

`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py` (+10 lines): `min(num_external_hit_tokens, max(request.num_tokens - 1, 0))` immediately after the lookup resolves and before `need_to_allocate` and `load_specs` are derived. The cap is idempotent against values the worker already truncated, preserves the async flag, and leaves every below cap result byte for byte unchanged.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

| Search | Result |
|---|---|
| Open PRs: "mooncake store cap", "MooncakeStore load_async=False" | Only #51358 (Mamba boundary state saves, unrelated) |
| Open PRs: "connector num_tokens - 1 cap" | None touching this method |
| #50864 (mine, scheduler side clamp for the same assert) | Closed in favor of this PR, per the review there that the fix belongs in the connector |

## Regression tests

Both tests fail with the fix stashed and pass with it applied.

| Test | What it proves |
|---|---|
| `test_full_prompt_lookup_capped_at_num_tokens_minus_one` | Connector side, existing `_StubLookupClient` pattern: lookup 32, computed 0, `num_tokens` 32 returns 31, async flag preserved, `load_specs` caches 31 |
| `test_full_prompt_lookup_does_not_crash_scheduler` | End to end through the real `Scheduler` and the real `MooncakeStoreConnector` scheduler side with only the ZMQ boundary stubbed and `load_async=False`: 32 token prompt schedules exactly 1 local token, `num_computed_tokens` reaches 32 (31 external + 1 local) |

## Test results (CPU only box, AMD 2 core)

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
# 24 passed (22 pre-existing + 2 new)

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_prepare_values.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
# 91 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake*.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
# 247 passed, 18 failed. The 18 are byte identical with and without this change (verified by stash flip on test names): pre-existing environment gaps (missing pytest-asyncio plugin, RDMA dependent worker paths).

.venv/bin/python -m ruff check <both touched files>   # All checks passed
.venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check <both files>  # already formatted
```

Additionally verified by direct calls: overshoot capped (32/32 to 31), sub cap values unchanged, `num_tokens=1` yields no phantom load, already truncated inputs pass through untouched (idempotent), and the async default path (`load_async=True`) still routes to `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` as designed with consistent cached accounting.

## Limitations and what CI should cover

No GPU on this box, so no serving or accuracy evals were possible. The change is CPU pure accounting (`min` on a token count) and only alters behavior where the scheduler previously asserted, but GPU validation of the disaggregated prefill path is requested. mypy was skipped (times out past 120s on this machine; no new typing surface was added).

items.title: [Test] Conformance suite for cache_salt across OpenAI entrypoints
items.body:
## Purpose

Implements the entrypoint axis of #53194, the half left open when @oneKn8 took
the tier axis in #53769. Tests only; no production file is touched.

`cache_salt` partitions the prefix cache only if it survives the whole trip from
an HTTP request body down to the block hasher. `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`
asserts that differing salts produce differing block hashes, but it builds
`Request` objects directly, so it begins after the plumbing that keeps
regressing.

Five cases over `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`:

- same prompt under two different salts must not reuse blocks
- same prompt under the same salt must reuse them
- a request that omits `cache_salt` must not land in a salted namespace
- the pooling path, which rebuilds prompts before they reach the hasher
- the pooling path with chunked preprocessing enabled — a strict xfail, below

Assertions read `vllm:prefix_cache_hits` rather than
`usage.prompt_tokens_details`, which is only populated under
`--enable-prompt-tokens-details` and is hard-coded to zero on the pooling path.
Nothing inspects the extra-key tuple, so this is unaffected by #44706, #51899,
#52655 and #43789, each of which changes that encoding.

## What each cited bug gets

Being precise about this, since the motivation is broader than the coverage:

| Bug | Covered here |
|---|---|
| #47696 pooling drops the salt | yes — strict xfail, currently failing |
| empty salt shared the unsalted namespace | yes — a plain passing arm. Found by @rishabhsinha17 reviewing this PR, and already fixed on main by #54353 (`min_length=1`) and #51444 (`validate_cache_salt`), so it pins the rejection rather than the bug |
| #51818 Harmony tool turns | no — the Responses API is not exercised; its bug is a continuation, needing a multi-turn case |
| #51748 HF3FS external keys | no — connector tier. `HF3FSKVConnector` is a *declared* rederiver in #53769's exempt map with an evidence pointer, but nothing in-tree executes that path, since CI cannot import the hf3fs client |

The Responses, Anthropic `/v1/messages`, classification and scoring endpoints
also accept `cache_salt` and are not covered. Worth follow-up.

## #47696 reproduces on current main

`test_chunked_embeddings_isolate_on_salt` is `xfail(strict=True)`, so it flips
to a loud XPASS when #47696 lands. Controlled A/B, two identical pooling
servers differing only in `pooler_config.enable_chunked_processing`, two trials
each:

```
config                              diff-salt  same-salt   verdict
enable_chunked_processing: false            0        128   isolated
                                            0        128   isolated
enable_chunked_processing: TRUE           128        128   128 victim tokens served
                                          128        128   128 victim tokens served
```

One detail wider than #47696's description: the prompt is 256 tokens against a
1024 `max_model_len`, so it is never actually split. Enabling the flag is
sufficient — every pooling request takes the rebuild path and loses the salt
whether or not chunking occurs, rather than only long inputs being affected.

## Every negative arm is paired with a positive control

Load-bearing rather than stylistic, and I have the receipt. An earlier revision
of the third case asserted only the miss. Run against a server started with
`--no-enable-prefix-caching`, the other cases failed as intended and **that one
still passed** — it would have shipped asserting nothing. It now also asserts
that two unsalted requests share with each other, so the miss it reports is the
salt boundary holding rather than the unsalted path never caching.

## Verification

Run against real servers on CPU, at 13cf9e0:

```
5 passed, 1 xfailed in 91.94s
```

Mutation-tested by disabling prefix caching, where every non-xfail case fails.

Two details came out of running it rather than reading:

- The CPU backend reuses `--gpu-memory-utilization` to size its KV cache from
  host RAM and defaults to 0.92, so the fixtures pin it low to stay runnable on
  a developer machine.
- The block size is deliberately not pinned. Supported kernel block sizes differ
  per attention backend (`vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`), and a fixed `--block-size 16`
  passed on CPU while failing to start elsewhere. Nothing here needs to know it.

The pooling arms serve a causal model under `--runner pooling` with `LAST`
pooling, because prefix caching applies to pooling only for last-token or all
pooling with causal attention. A conventional bidirectional embedding model
would never engage the cache, and those arms would pass without testing
anything.

This file is standalone rather than importing `dimensions.py` from #53769, so
the two can merge in either order. Unifying them once both land would be an
improvement.

cc @oneKn8 @rishabhsinha17

items.body:
## Summary

Generalizes the offloading connector's declarative stats into `kv_connector/v1/metrics.py` so any connector can report metrics without a per-connector `KVConnectorStats` / `KVConnectorPromMetrics` subclass:

- `MetricMetadata` / `CounterMetadata` / `GaugeMetadata` / `HistogramMetadata` (moved from `vllm/v1/kv_offload/base.py`; the `Offloading*Metadata` names remain as aliases).
- `TypedKVConnectorStats`: the self-describing `{types, data}` payload with `increase_counter` / `set_gauge` / `observe_histogram`, and type-driven `aggregate` / `reduce` / `is_empty`. `OffloadingConnectorStats` is now an alias of it.
- `TypedKVConnectorPromMetrics`: registers one Prometheus metric per definition and records payloads by metric type. `OffloadPromMetrics` subclasses it and only keeps the deprecated `transfer_type`-labelled CPU offload metrics.

Because every connector using this shares one concrete stats type keyed by metric name, metrics from different families compose by recording into the same instance (or aggregating), and `MultiConnector` continues to work unchanged. Nixl / Mooncake / HF3FS keep their bespoke stats classes; the base interface does not change.

The next PR in this stack (HiSparse cache metrics) is the first non-offloading user.

Not duplicating an open PR: searched open PRs for "KVConnectorStats", "typed"/"declarative" connector metrics, and "connector metrics definitions"; #50878 (external metrics providers for stat logger plugins) and #41790 (SimpleCPU offload metrics) are unrelated.

items.title: [Security] Bind LMCache token keys to media hash, cache salt, and LoRA
items.body:
## Summary
The in-tree LMCache connector derived external cache keys from prompt token IDs after overwriting multimodal placeholders with a 16-bit truncation of the media identifier, and it never mixed `cache_salt` or LoRA identity into those keys. Distinct media that shared the low 16 hash bits, or requests that differed only in salt or adapter, could therefore hit or overwrite each other's stored KV. This change writes a 63-bit media identifier into placeholder spans and XOR-mixes cache salt and LoRA name into every token on both the scheduler lookup path and the worker store path.

## Changes
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/lmcache_token_keys.py`: new helpers for full-width media identifiers and request-identity mixing.
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/lmcache_integration/utils.py`: re-export the binder used by the native adapter.
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/lmcache_integration/vllm_v1_adapter.py`: apply the binder in `get_num_new_matched_tokens` and `ReqMeta.from_request_tracker`.
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py`: carry `cache_salt` on `NewRequestData` so store-side keying can see it.

## Codepath coverage
- Scheduler lookup (`get_num_new_matched_tokens`) and worker/store metadata (`ReqMeta.from_request_tracker`) both call the same binder.
- HTTP, SageMaker `/invocations`, gRPC, and batch all become `Request` objects that hit those two methods when `LMCacheConnectorV1` is enabled.
- Unsalted, non-LoRA text-only keys are unchanged. Existing multimodal LMCache entries are invalidated by the wider identifier, which is intended.
- The default `use_native=False` path still loads `lmcache.integration.vllm.vllm_v1_adapter` from the external `lmcache` package; that copy needs the same binding upstream. This PR fixes the in-tree native adapter (`use_native=True`) and the helpers vLLM owns.

## Duplicate-work check
Searched open and merged PRs for `hex_hash_to_int16`, `apply_mm_hashes_to_token_ids`, `lmcache_integration`, `cache_salt lmcache`, and `LMCacheConnectorV1 hash`. Nearby open work is on other connectors or LMCache-MP (`#54342` HF3FS, `#53496` ExampleConnector, `#45549`/`#44097`/`#40041` LMCache-MP). None of those close 16-bit media truncation or dropped salt/LoRA on the in-process LMCache token-id key.

## Tests
- `test_mm_hashes_sharing_low_16_bits_are_distinct`: identifiers that collide in 16 bits stay distinct after binding.
- `test_cache_salt_and_lora_partition_lmcache_token_keys`: different salts/adapters produce different keys; unsalted text-only tokens are unchanged.
- `test_store_and_lookup_apply_the_same_lmcache_token_binding`: lookup and store helpers emit identical keys.
- `test_from_request_copies_cache_salt`: `NewRequestData` carries the request salt.

items.title: [Test] Conformance suite for KV-cache key partitioning
items.body:
## Purpose

Implements the tier axis of #53194, plus a registry coverage gate. Tests only; no production file is touched.

The RFC observes that every fix for a dropped partitioning dimension (`cache_salt`, `lora_name`, `prompt_embeds`, ...) has shipped with its own bespoke test, so the *next* dimension and the *next* cache tier get no coverage for free. I offered a split in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53194#issuecomment-5389653956: @Tejasvichand keeps the `dimension x entrypoint` HTTP matrix he volunteered for, and this PR takes the other half, `dimension x tier`, which needs no server.

The invariant under test, stated once in `dimensions.py` and applied everywhere: two requests that differ in a partitioning dimension must never reuse each other's blocks, and two that agree in it must. The positive control matters as much as the negative one, since a cache that never reuses anything trivially satisfies the safety half.

Adding a dimension is one `Dimension` entry and it is immediately asserted against every tier. Adding a tier is one harness. Nothing in the suite inspects the extra-key tuple, so it stays independent of how the keys are encoded and does not need updating when the encoding changes.

### The gate

A parametrized suite over a hardcoded list of tiers has exactly the weakness it is meant to replace: a connector added tomorrow simply is not in the list. `test_tier_coverage_gate.py` walks `KVConnectorFactory._registry` and fails on any built-in connector that is neither exercised by the suite nor exempted with a written reason. Registering a connector without declaring how it partitions the keyspace breaks the build rather than passing silently. Test-registered mock connectors are classified out by their loader's module path.

The exemption list is the part reviewers should push back on: today 14 of the 16 built-in connectors are exempt, almost all because they need a GPU or a third-party package. I would rather that be a visible list with reasons than an invisible gap.

It pushed back. @rishabhsinha17 pointed out on #53194 that a dependency reason ("needs a mooncake store") was standing in for a keying claim nobody had written down, so an exemption now also declares the connector's `Keying` shape with the `path:line` it was read from. Exempt means "CI cannot execute this", not "nobody has said what this does". Filling that table meant reading all fourteen, which is how `HF3FSKVConnector` ended up in it as a re-deriver: it chains `md5(f"{previous_hash}_{token_ids}")` over `request.prompt_token_ids` and its directory contains no reference to `cache_salt` or `lora` at all. The `cache_salt` half is #51748; the LoRA half is wider than that issue.

Two rules make the declarations load-bearing rather than decorative. A `REDERIVES` exemption must cite the issue tracking it, so a connector that drops every dimension cannot be parked behind a missing dependency. And `COVERED` is derived from the harness manifest rather than restated, so "covered" means a harness actually runs the connector instead of a string claiming one does.

### The xfails are the point

Every mark is `strict=True` at an explicit call site, so each fails the build the moment its bug is fixed and nobody remembers to delete it:

- `test_cross_dimension_equal_strings_never_reuse_blocks` reproduces #44701 on CPU: `cache_salt="shared"` and `lora_name="shared"` hash identically because the extra keys carry no domain separation. Fixed by #51899, so this mark comes off when that lands.
- The five `ExampleConnector` arms reproduce #53495, which I filed off the back of writing this suite. That connector re-derives its storage key from raw prompt tokens instead of consuming `request.block_hashes`, so it drops *every* dimension at once and keys `prompt_embeds` requests on an empty prompt. #53496 fixes it, and these marks come off with it.
- The `lora_version` arms reproduce #42125 in-engine, fixed by #48352.

The first thesis is the one the `ExampleConnector` contrast encodes: a connector must not re-derive the cache key, because consuming `request.block_hashes` is correct in every dimension, present and future, at no cost.

The `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector-lora_version` arm is the sharper one, and I owe the framing to @Tejasvichand. That connector consumes `request.block_hashes` faithfully, exactly as the paragraph above argues every connector should, and it *still* serves the previous adapter's blocks, because the canonical key it consumes is the one that dropped the dimension. Consuming the canonical key is necessary and not sufficient: a connector is complete precisely when the engine hash is, and no earlier. That is the argument for asserting both tiers rather than picking one, and it is why the connector tier is not merely the in-engine tier restated one layer out.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/conformance/ -q
```

CPU-only, no GPU and no server. Runs in about 7 seconds.

## Test Result

```
26 passed, 8 xfailed in 7.3s
```

On this branch at 81803401, based on main at 299ebd09. The 8 xfails are the five `ExampleConnector` arms, the in-engine and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` `lora_version` arms, and the cross-dimension collision; all are `strict=True` at an explicit mark site rather than relying on an `xfail_strict` ini default, and all currently reproduce real bugs on main.

Independently reproduced by @Tejasvichand on macOS/arm64 at 24 passed / 8 xfailed for the tree at 3a3283a5, an architecture this repo's CI does not cover.

Verified against #53496 on an RTX A6000: with that fix applied, the 4 `ExampleConnector` arms XPASS (strict), which is the suite failing loudly and correctly, and is why those marks are tied to that PR merging (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53496#issuecomment-5402042290).

The gate currently passes, i.e. every built-in connector in the registry is either covered or has a written exemption.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Retire in-flight output state on load-failure recompute
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #45138. When KV-load-failure recompute truncates a request's `num_computed_tokens` at the first invalid block, the scheduler now also retires the request's in-flight output state: output placeholders are zeroed, drafted spec tokens are cleared, and outputs still in flight from the invalid KV are marked stale so they drain and drop as they return instead of landing as valid tokens.

## Claims

- `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` retires in-flight output state for every affected request, using the same `drop_stale_output` / `num_stale_output_tokens` idiom as `_handle_stopped_request`: in-flight outputs from invalid KV are dropped on return, placeholders restart at zero, and spec drafts are rebound to empty.
- Stale placeholders no longer leak into the scheduling arithmetic after recompute. That leak is what inflated `num_new_tokens` and stranded requests in the running queue in #45138.
- The reset is a no-op for requests with nothing in flight (sync scheduling, or async loads still waiting for remote KV), so non-failure paths are untouched.

## Validation

New regression test `test_sync_recompute_retires_inflight_output_state` builds the failure state directly: a running request with one outstanding placeholder share beyond the current step's, drafted spec tokens, and an invalid block reported mid-prompt. It asserts the truncated frontier, zeroed placeholders, exactly one stale share still outstanding with drop mode on (this step's share drains in lockstep inside `update_from_output`), and that the draft list is rebound rather than mutated.

Commands and results (CPU, macOS, worktree at 592c6f3fbc):

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py -q
# 4 passed (3 pre-existing + 1 new)

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ -q \
  --ignore=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  --ignore=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py
# 1710 passed, 10 failed, 40 skipped
# All 10 failures reproduce identically on pristine upstream/main
# (verified via git stash on this branch): test_hf3fs_connector (4),
# test_hisparse_connector (2), test_multi_connector (1),
# test_nixl_connector_hma (1), test_offloading_connector (2).
# They are environment issues on this machine, unrelated to this change.

ruff check / ruff format --check on both touched files: clean
```

The two ignored modules fail collection on this machine for missing `ray`, unrelated to this change. End-to-end repro would need a GPU deployment with a KV connector reporting block-level load failures; not available here, so validation is at the scheduler unit level, matching how the neighboring invalid-block tests cover this code.

## Details

Root cause: the recompute path rewinds `num_computed_tokens` but left the request's output-side state untouched. Under async scheduling a request can have placeholders and in-flight sampled outputs at the moment the failure surfaces; those outputs were sampled from KV that is now known-invalid, and the leftover placeholders kept counting into `num_new_tokens` projections, which is the stranding mechanism reported in #45138.

Why not the existing PRs:

- #45146 fixes the placeholder half of this on an older tree and has been inactive since June. It does not touch in-flight outputs or spec drafts.
- #49252 covers the `num_computed_tokens` truncation for sync + async loads and has been stalled since August; its substance is largely absorbed by the current `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` rewrite, and it also leaves output-side state alone.
- This PR supersedes my own earlier #45430 (closed), redone against current main using the stale-output machinery that landed since (`num_in_flight_tokens` / `num_stale_output_tokens` / `drop_stale_output`), which keeps the fix to nine lines in the scheduler by reusing the drain loop in `update_from_output`.

items.title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Key ExampleConnector storage on block hashes
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53495.

`ExampleConnector` derived its storage key from the raw prompt token bytes, in three places: the scheduler-side lookup (`_found_match_for_request`), the metadata builder (`_found_match_for_prompt`), and again on the worker at save and load time (`_generate_filename_debug`). That key ignores `cache_salt`, LoRA identity and `prompt_embeds` content, so a request with a different salt or adapter was handed another request's KV (three full blocks in the reproduction), and `prompt_embeds` requests, whose `prompt_token_ids` is `None`, all keyed on the empty prompt and reported a negative match count (`align_to_block_size(-1, 16) == -16`).

The key is now derived once, on the scheduler side, from the hash of the last cached block in `request.block_hashes`. The block hash chain already binds tokens, `cache_salt`, LoRA, multimodal items and `prompt_embeds`, so nothing is re-derived: `update_state_after_alloc` records the key, `ReqMeta` carries it, and the worker only joins it to a path. Store and load now also agree on the cached-token count, which the old code aligned two different ways (`align(len)` on store, `align(len - 1)` on lookup), so prompts of length `k * block_size + 1` could never hit.

This is the pattern the connectors that already partition correctly use: `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` and `OffloadingConnector` key on `request.block_hashes`. It is the same defect class as #51748 (HF3FS) and the one #53194 proposes a conformance suite for.

Net diff: +73 / -101 in the connector, no interface change outside `ReqMeta` / `ExampleConnectorMetadata.add_request`, which have no other in-tree callers (`ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` has its own metadata types).

## Test Plan

New `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector_keying.py`, CPU only, no model: for each of `cache_salt`, LoRA and `prompt_embeds`, store request A through the connector's real scheduler and worker path (`update_state_after_alloc`, `build_connector_meta`, `save_kv_layer` on a CPU tensor), then assert `get_num_new_matched_tokens` for B is a full hit when B agrees with A and zero when it differs, plus unset-vs-set, a short-prompt case, and the `num_computed_tokens` offset.

Duplicate check run per AGENTS.md: no open PR references #53495 or touches `example_connector.py` keying; searched `ExampleConnector cache_salt`, `example_connector block_hashes`, `SharedStorageConnector cache_salt`.

## Test Result

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector_keying.py -q
9 passed in 2.88s
```

On `main` the same cases give `48` for the different-salt and different-LoRA arms and `-16` for `prompt_embeds`.

Related existing tests, same result with and without the change: `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py`, `test_multi_connector.py` (one pre-existing failure from a gated HF repo, identical on `main`), `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "connector or kv_transfer or external"` (27 pre-existing failures from model inspection on a CPU-only box, identical set on `main`).

The connector tier of the #53194 conformance suite (branch https://github.com/oneKn8/vllm/tree/kv-partitioning-conformance) marks the five ExampleConnector arms `xfail(strict=True)`; with this change they all XPASS on current main, which is the intended flip.

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector.py` (the GPU e2e test asserting unique storage folders per image set) is unchanged; multimodal identifiers are part of the block hash, so the folder-count expectations hold. I cannot run it locally (no GPU), so I would appreciate a `ready` label for CI.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

---

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Unblock scheduling after a failed async KV load
items.body:
## Overview

With `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, a request whose async KV load fails with no usable prefix can sit in WAITING forever, even on an idle engine, and the requests queued behind it never run. Nothing errors. It takes a connector that offers the same async load again on the retry, e.g. MooncakeStoreConnector (async by default) or a MultiConnector whose offloading child holds the prefix after NIXL fails.

Related: #59096, #59099, #59102, #59325, #59329 (independent fixes in nearby KV load paths).

## Claims

- The failed request is admitted again once its load fits.
- Requests holding loaded blocks are no longer stuck behind it.
- No change when the failed load keeps a valid prefix.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py -q
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/core -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

On main the two no-prefix cases fail (`assert <RequestStatus.WAITING: 1> == <RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS: 3>`) and the three-request case schedules neither loaded request (`assert 'id-7' in {}`); the valid-prefix control passes. With the fix all 18 tests in the file pass, and either half of the fix alone leaves a test red.

Suites, macOS arm64 (CPU), with the fix:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit`: 1905 passed, 12 failed, 42 skipped
- `tests/v1/core`: 919 passed, 1 failed, 4 errors

Without the scheduler change (new tests kept), `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` gives 1902 passed and 15 failed: the same 12 plus the 3 new tests. `tests/v1/core` is unchanged. The other 12 and the core failures also fail on unmodified main here: NVIDIA-only paths (hf3fs, HiSparse, offloading tiering), Ray on the CPU platform, a gated model, and end-to-end tests that need more free RAM than this machine had.

CPU only: the tests drive the real Scheduler with a mocked connector, as the rest of this file does. No GPU run.

## Details

After the failure, `_update_waiting_for_remote_kv` frees the request's blocks ([scheduler.py:3097](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L3097)) but leaves it in `_inflight_prefills` and `kv_holding_waiting`.

- Async admission reserves the remaining blocks of every in-flight prefill (#44560, [scheduler.py:1214](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1214-L1217)). Holding nothing, the request now reserves its whole sequence against its own retry, so the gate ([kv_cache_manager.py:575](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L575-L579)) needs room for the load plus its full size. In the test: 10 usable blocks, a 6-block prompt, a 5-block hit, and 10 - 6 < 5 on every step.
- `kv_holding_waiting` is drained first so that a block holder never waits behind a request whose failed allocation stops the scan (#58947). The freed request is exactly that request.

The fix discards it from `_inflight_prefills` when its blocks are freed, as preemption does, and moves a request that no longer holds blocks (by `_holds_kv_blocks`, which the queues already route by) from `kv_holding_waiting` to the front of `waiting` before scheduling it. The reservation itself is unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes these lines on current main. #55297 makes MooncakeStore's next lookup a miss after an invalid-block failure; it is complementary and leaves the scheduler state, `failed_recving` and other connectors as they are. #57418 and #59343 use the reservation without touching this path; #53298, #54733 and #56733 handle sync or hybrid failures, and #59603 forwards failed loads to LMCache's scheduler side.

## AI assistance

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to audit this code path, write the fix and write the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself. The commit carries a Co-authored-by trailer, as AGENTS.md asks.

items.title: [Feature][Observability] Add production-ready Grafana dashboards
items.body:
## Overview

Adds five Grafana dashboards for vLLM's Prometheus metrics to `examples/observability/dashboards/grafana/`. **Service Status** is a large-print status board for the people who use a vLLM service. The other four are for the team that runs it: **Overview** (with latency SLOs), an **Instances** drill-down, **KV Cache**, and **Speculative Decoding**. The PR also updates the dashboard READMEs and adds a short *Grafana Dashboards* section to `docs/usage/metrics.md`.

The existing dashboards (`performance_statistics.json`, `query_statistics.json`, `prometheus_grafana/grafana.json`) and the Perses specs are unchanged. There are no Python code changes. No issue is linked; see *Duplicate-work check* under Details.

## Claims

- **Coverage:** the new dashboards chart 69 `vllm:*` metrics; the three existing Grafana examples chart 17 between them. The added coverage includes:
  - per-engine (data-parallel) views and SLO attainment
  - prefix caching by cache tier, KV block residency, KV connectors (NIXL) and KV offloading
  - speculative decoding, sleep mode, LoRA and MFU
  - the API server's HTTP and process metrics
- **Built for fleets:** every panel aggregates across instances and engines. Variables cover data source, job, model, instance and engine, plus ad hoc filters such as `namespace`. The dashboards link to each other and keep the time range and filters. Clicking a row in the per-model or per-instance table drills down to it.
- **Robust queries:**
  - ratios are guarded against division by zero
  - quantiles are computed from summed bucket rates
  - token-length panels use only the bucket boundaries that all selected servers share
  - the status board shows *Down*, and blanks its numbers instead of freezing them, as soon as a model's servers stop reporting
- **End-user view:** `vLLM / Service Status` shows one strip per model with Status (Online / Sleeping / Down), response time, output speed, success rate and requests per minute. The tiles are color-coded, readable from across a room, and work in kiosk mode.
- **Compatibility:** Grafana 10.4+ (tested on 10.4, 11.6 and 13.2) and Prometheus 2.26+ (including 3.x, Thanos and Mimir). Every queried metric name is defined on `main`.

## Validation

| Check | Setup | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Metric names | Every `vllm:*` series name the dashboards query (108, including `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count`), checked against the metric definitions in `vllm/` on upstream `main` (8a26869) and in the nightly wheel | 108 / 108 defined |
| Real servers | Nightly CPU wheel `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d` on 4 vCPUs. `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with n-gram speculative decoding, and `distilbert/distilgpt2` with `--kv-cache-metrics`. Prometheus 3.15.0, 5 s scrape. About 40 min of mixed traffic: streaming and non-streaming requests, shared prefixes, client aborts and invalid requests | 169 / 223 queries return data, 0 errors. The other 54 need features this setup doesn't run: LoRA, sleep mode, KV connectors / offloading, multimodal cache, and block reuse (none sampled) |
| Rendering, real servers | All five dashboards with every row expanded, in headless Chromium, on Grafana 13.2.3, 11.6.16 and 10.4.19 | 0 panel errors and 0 page errors on each version. *No data* appears only on the optional-feature panels listed above |
| Outage | Stopped and restarted the distilgpt2 server | Its status tile showed *Down* within one scrape and its other tiles went blank, with no stale values. It returned to *Online* after the restart, and the status timeline recorded the outage |
| Optional features | Simulated fleet: 3 servers, 2 models, data-parallel engines, and 1 unreachable target. vLLM's own `PrometheusStatLogger` and connector metric classes are driven with synthetic stats for sleep mode, weight updates, LoRA, spec decode, NIXL, `OffloadingConnector` and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` | 221 / 223 queries return data (the 2 empty ones are the multimodal cache hit rate, which isn't simulated). On all three Grafana versions every panel renders with data, with 0 errors |
| Lint | `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | typos and markdownlint pass |

**Screenshots.** These were taken on the real servers in Grafana 13.2.3, between 03:05 and 03:45 UTC. distilgpt2 was stopped at 03:13 and was back by 03:16. The servers run on CPU, so latencies are high, and the red 9 tok/s output-speed tile for Qwen is the expected result.

![vLLM / Service Status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/service-status.png)

| vLLM / Overview | vLLM / Instances |
| --- | --- |
| ![vLLM / Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/overview.png) | ![vLLM / Instances](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/instances.png) |
| **vLLM / KV Cache** | **vLLM / Speculative Decoding** |
| ![vLLM / KV Cache](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/kv-cache.png) | ![vLLM / Speculative Decoding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/speculative-decoding.png) |

The real-server run found two bugs, which are fixed in the last commit:
- The prompt/output length distribution added up to 177%, because request-token bucket boundaries scale with `--max-model-len` and the two models used different values.
- Grafana 13 threw an uncaught error for ad hoc filters on a templated data source. Defaulting the Data source variable to `default` fixes it.

![Prompt and output length distribution, before and after the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gaby/vllm/172849090a95db18230e66a1bb4af0e4454c4b6a/pr-454/length-distribution-fix.png)

**Model evaluation:** not applicable. The PR adds dashboard JSON and docs only; model outputs and serving are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction (real servers)</summary>

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12
uv pip install vllm \
  "triton @ https://github.com/triton-lang/triton-cpu/releases/download/v3.8.0/triton-3.8.0+cpu-cp312-abi3-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl" \
  --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cpu --index-strategy first-index --torch-backend cpu

VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=2 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "prompt_lookup_max": 3, "prompt_lookup_min": 2}'
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=2 vllm serve distilbert/distilgpt2 --port 8001 \
  --kv-cache-metrics --kv-cache-metrics-sample 1.0
```

- Prometheus scrapes both servers every 5 s.
- Grafana has a Prometheus data source and a file provider pointing at `examples/observability/dashboards/grafana`.
- Traffic comes from 6 async clients on `/v1/completions`: 70% streaming, a shared ~600-token prefix, repetitive text for n-gram drafts, 5% client aborts and 3% invalid requests.
- Every query was run through the Prometheus HTTP API with the variables set to *All*. A Playwright script rendered each dashboard with its rows expanded and checked every panel for errors.

</details>

## Details

**Motivation.** The existing examples have 13–16 panels each and chart 17 metrics between them, mostly request latency and throughput. They have no instance or engine dimension, no SLO view, and nothing aimed at the people who use the service.

**Design.**
- **Format and naming.** The dashboards are plain Grafana JSON (schemaVersion 39), so they work with UI import, the HTTP API or file provisioning. They are prefixed `vllm_`, tagged `vllm`, and have stable `vllm-*` uids so links between them work. The existing dashboards are kept so current imports keep working.
- **Optional features.** Rows for optional features are collapsed, and their titles name the flag they need (for example *requires --kv-cache-metrics*).
- **SLO tiles.** These count requests below a histogram bucket boundary, so the selectable targets are default boundaries; other targets need `--custom-histogram-buckets`, which the docs explain.
- **Status board.**
  - Tiles are instant queries that only return a value while the model is reporting.
  - *Output speed* is generated tokens per second divided by the average number of running requests. Unlike 1/TPOT, it counts every token of a speculative decoding step.
  - The color thresholds (1 / 3 s, 10 / 20 tok/s, 95 / 99 %) are defaults to tune.
- **Diff size.** Almost all of the diff is dashboard JSON (11,853 lines). The docs change is 120 added and 50 removed lines.

**Limitations.**
- No CI check covers the dashboards, so a renamed metric would not be caught automatically. The metric-name check above was run by hand.
- Real-server validation ran on CPU, not on a GPU deployment. GPU-only features (sleep mode, NIXL, offloading) are covered only by the simulator.
- Ray metrics (`RayPrometheusStatLogger`) use other names and are not covered. The Perses specs are not updated.
- HTTP and process metrics are not labelled by model, and process metrics are missing with `--api-server-count` > 1. The README documents both.
- Not charted: HiSparse, Mooncake store, HF3FS, KV-offload tiering, diffusion, realtime WebSocket and tool-parser metrics.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Evict invalid blocks of requests aborted mid-step
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61768. A request aborted in the same step its synchronous KV load fails leaves the scheduler before the failure report is processed, so its never-loaded blocks stay prefix-cache hits. This keeps the departing request's block ids until its in-flight outputs arrive, and evicts them when a late failure report names them.

## Claims

- After a sync KV load failure whose owner was aborted in the same step, the invalid block and every block after it are evicted, under both `kv_load_failure_policy` values and with sync and async scheduling. With async scheduling or PP this relies on deferred freeing, which is on for a top-level `kv_consumer`/`kv_both`; see Tradeoffs and limits for a top-level producer whose connector loads.
- A later identical prompt recomputes instead of decoding from never-loaded KV (GPU: r2 cached 1904 → 0, output matches the full-recompute baseline).
- An abort whose load succeeded keeps its valid cached KV (unchanged behavior).

## Validation

**Tests** (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py`). The four regression tests fail on main at the eviction assertion; with this change all of them pass:

| Test | Role |
|---|---|
| `test_aborted_sync_load_invalid_suffix_evicted` (policy × delayed connector free × PP 1/2) | regression: evicts from the first invalid block; next request hits only the valid prefix |
| `test_aborted_load_survives_other_queued_step` | regression: a batch without a failure keeps the blocks; the later failing batch evicts them |
| `test_aborted_load_survives_empty_schedule` | regression: an empty schedule between the load step and its output keeps the record |
| `test_aborted_sharer_suffix_evicted_by_earlier_batch_failure` | regression: a finished request computed over a block that failed in an earlier batch |
| `test_aborted_successful_sync_load_preserves_cache` | guard: an abort with a successful load keeps the cache |
| `test_finished_request_retained_until_all_outputs_processed` | lifecycle: under async scheduling a record lives until its last in-flight output |

`assert_scheduler_empty` in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py` now also checks the record is empty, so existing tests guard against leaks.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py   # 25 passed
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" pytest --timeout=300 tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ tests/v1/core/
```

The second command ran on this branch and on main at the same commit (`81e1c3f1`) without this change, with the GPU hidden: the precompiled kernels available locally are for an older commit, so GPU tests can't run meaningfully here and are left to CI. This branch: 2911 passed, 217 failed, 112 errors. Main: 2889 passed, 239 failed, 112 errors. **No test fails on this branch that passes on main.** The only difference is the 22 new tests, which fail on main. The 329 shared failures and errors are mostly tests that need a device, plus a few that already fail on main; all of them fail identically there:

<details>
<summary>Shared failures and errors by file (identical on main without this change)</summary>
